cases.intent: Empty input returns an empty list.
Repeated separators, ordinary whitespace, and empty quoted labels are discarded.
Outside commas separate labels and empty segments do not affect first occurrence order.
Quotes toggle anywhere, disappear, and concatenate adjacent quoted and unquoted uppercase text.
Quoted commas are literal, including repeated commas and commas at label boundaries.
Outside quotes, escaped comma, quote, backslash, and uppercase letter each emit exactly one literal character.
Inside quotes, escaped punctuation does not toggle mode and escaped uppercase still lowercases.
All six ordinary ASCII whitespace characters trim at boundaries and collapse together internally.
All six quoted whitespace characters and their repeated multiplicity survive as a nonempty label.
Escaping each of the six ASCII whitespace characters protects them outside quotes.
Trim only surrounding ordinary whitespace while preserving quoted boundary spaces, tabs, CR, and internal spaces.
Escaped boundary spaces survive after adjacent ordinary boundary whitespace is trimmed.
Protected whitespace breaks ordinary runs; each neighboring ordinary run collapses independently.
An escaped space or tab between ordinary runs is preserved and prevents merging those runs.
Empty quote pairs emit nothing, so ordinary whitespace across them forms one run and still trims at boundaries.
Deduplicate equal outputs after concatenation, lowercasing, trimming, collapsing, and escaping.
Protected-only labels remain nonempty; deduplication compares characters rather than protection provenance or whitespace similarity.
Non-whitespace ASCII controls, digits, punctuation, and single quotes remain literal while uppercase lowercases.
An escaped backslash consumes exactly one character, leaving the following comma active and permitting a literal final backslash.
A trailing unpaired escape invalidates the whole input after valid and duplicate labels.
A trailing escape inside quoted mode invalidates the entire input after a valid label.
A quote opened midway through a later label invalidates the whole input despite valid preceding labels and embedded commas.
An escaped final quote stays literal and cannot close quoted mode after otherwise valid labels.

rationale: These 23 deterministic ASCII cases cover all ten rules and their interactions. Successful expectations follow left-to-right quote and escape handling, removal of quote delimiters, trimming only ordinary boundary whitespace, independent collapse of ordinary runs, exact preservation of protected whitespace, ASCII lowercasing, empty-result removal, and exact deduplication in first occurrence order. They exercise all six whitespace characters in ordinary, quoted, and escaped forms, protected boundaries and run breaks, empty quote concatenation, literal punctuation and controls, and equality across protection provenance. Four invalid suffix cases require whole-input ValueError even after valid labels. No Unicode or non-string behavior is tested.
